00001| ---
00002| title: unstable_cache
00003| description: API Reference for the unstable_cache function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| > **Note:**
00007| > This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.
00008| > We recommend opting into [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and replacing `unstable_cache` with the `use cache` directive.
00009| 
00010| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
00011| 
00012| ```jsx
00013| import { getUser } from './data';
00014| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
00015| 
00016| const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00017|   async (id) => getUser(id),
00018|   ['my-app-user']
00019| );
00020| 
00021| export default async function Component({ userID }) {
00022|   const user = await getCachedUser(userID);
00023|   ...
00024| }
00025| ```
00026| 
00027| > **Good to know**:
00028| >
00029| > - Accessing request data such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. Read the data outside the cached function and pass the values you need as arguments.
00030| > - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
00031| 
00032| ## Unsupported operations
00033| 
00034| The function passed to `unstable_cache` cannot depend on the incoming request. Read values from `cookies()` or `headers()` before calling the cached function, then pass those values as arguments so they become part of the cache key.
00035| 
00036| The cached function also cannot:
00037| 
00038| - Call `connection()`, which requires an incoming request
00039| - Enable or disable draft mode
00040| - Call `revalidateTag()`, `updateTag()`, or `revalidatePath()` during cache execution
00041| - Call a function that uses the `use cache: private` directive
00042| 
00043| Perform request-dependent work before calling the cached function. Perform mutations and revalidation afterward from a Server Action or Route Handler.
00044| 
00045| ## Parameters
00046| 
00047| ```jsx
00048| const data = unstable_cache(fetchData, keyParts, options)()
00049| ```
00050| 
00051| - `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.
00052| - `keyParts`: This is an extra array of keys that further adds identification to the cache. By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. It is optional in most cases; the only time you need to use it is when you use external variables without passing them as parameters. However, it is important to add closures used within the function if you do not pass them as parameters.
00053| - `options`: This is an object that controls how the cache behaves. It can contain the following properties:
00054|   - `tags`: An array of tags that can be used to control cache invalidation. Next.js will not use this to uniquely identify the function.
00055|   - `revalidate`: The number of seconds after which the cache should be revalidated. Omit or pass `false` to cache indefinitely or until matching `revalidateTag()` or `revalidatePath()` methods are called.
00056| 
00057| ## Returns
00058| 
00059| `unstable_cache` returns a function that when invoked, returns a Promise that resolves to the cached data. If the data is not in the cache, the provided function will be invoked, and its result will be cached and returned.
00060| 
00061| ## Example
00062| 
00063| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00064| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00065| 
00066| export default async function Page({
00067|   params,
00068| }: {
00069|   params: Promise<{ userId: string }>
00070| }) {
00071|   const { userId } = await params
00072|   const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00073|     async () => {
00074|       return { id: userId }
00075|     },
00076|     [userId], // add the user ID to the cache key
00077|     {
00078|       tags: ['users'],
00079|       revalidate: 60,
00080|     }
00081|   )
00082| 
00083|   //...
00084| }
00085| ```
00086| 
00087| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00088| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

>

title: use server
description: Learn how to use the use server directive to execute code on the server.
---

The `use server` directive designates a function or file to be executed on the **server side**. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all functions in the file are server-side, or inline at the top of a function to mark the function as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This is a React feature.

For Next.js-specific Server Action behaviors (response model, security, configuration, deployment), see [Server Actions and Mutations](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).

## Using `use server` at the top of a file

The following example shows a file with a `use server` directive at the top. All functions in the file are executed on the server.

```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
'use server'

part.text:
I have implemented the admin product catalog page with cached catalog data and background revalidation:

- **Catalog Caching:** Wrapped `getAllProducts` using `unstable_cache` with cache tag `"products"` to avoid re-querying upstream catalog data on every request.
- **Background Revalidation:** Configured the catalog synchronization trigger to call `revalidateTag("products", "max")` in an inline Server Action (`'use server'`). The `"max"` profile serves stale cached data while revalidating in the background (stale-while-revalidate), preventing the admin experience from blocking on large SKU recalculations.
- **Form Action:** Implemented a regular HTML `<form>` using the inline Server Action with a `"Sync latest catalog"` submit button.
